newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India grinds to a halt in London trade.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India grinds to a halt in London trade.

text.p: A slide on the Bombay bourse after a five percent rise yesterday resulted in thin directionless trade in London.
"There is nothing really going on. People are waiting for the end of what has been a horrible year," said one trader.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 0.02 points at 56.46 points, with the premium over the local market at 16.24 percent compared with yesterday's 13.05 percent.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index fell 61.10 points, or 2.08 percent, to 2,880.26.
Bombay gave up its gains after talk of plans to give up new corporate taxes evaporated.
"No one thought they were going to give back the tax," said the trader.
The GDRs had in any case moved before the five percent gain on the BSE on the back of buying out of the U.S. earlier in the week.
Today, individual stocks rallied on the back of the thinnest of orders, with Bajaj Auto up $1.91 at $26.00/$27.50.
"Traders are running flat books. You see an order come in and then people trying to cover it, which is why Bajaj is now on a 34 percent premium to the underlying," said a trader.
Hindalco came off after a week long rally in its GDRs, to close down 52 cents at $20.25/$21.25.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.18 points at 61.03, a premium of 35.93 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index fell 15.30 points, 2.17 percent, to a provisional 689.38.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended rose 1.71 points, 1.85 percent, to 93.91, a premium of 3.99 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index rose 22.88 points to 6,825.62.
